summary: Seán McLoughlin works in religious studies and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Manchester and served as a Lecturer in South Asian, Islamic and Religious Studies at the University of Leeds (attested 2005).

Shagun Sinha works in Indology, computational linguistics, and linguistics. He completed his PhD at Jawaharlal Nehru University under doctoral supervisor Girish Nath Jha (attested 2022) alongside several other teachers.

Shailendra Bhandare specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. He has held positions as a curator at the British Museum, a fellow at the Fitzwilliam Museum, Fellow at St Cross College (attested 2022), and Assistant Keeper at the Ashmolean Museum (attested 2006-2022).

Shailja Singh studied for an MBBS at Jawaharlal Nehru Medical College, Aligarh (2019-2025). Working in Indology and other fields, she became Concurrent Faculty at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2026).

Shaman Hatley works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Goddard College and completed his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania (~2000-2007) under Harunaga Isaacson. He taught at Concordia University (~2007-2015) and joined the University of Massachusetts Boston in 2015.
Shan Shan Zhao works in Buddhist studies. She earned a Master of Arts at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn, also studying with Shayne Clarke and Mark Rowe.

Shanshan Jia works in Indology and Tibetology. She studied as a doctoral student under Harunaga Isaacson at the University of Hamburg (attested 2015, 2026), where she is also a Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin (attested 2026).
Shantanu Nevrekar works in Indology and other fields. He was a PhD candidate in anthropology at Stanford University (2019-2026) and served as Visiting Faculty at Ashoka University in 2026.
Shanti Bhikshu Shastri (1912-2003) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Friedrich Weller, taught Wilhelm Rau, and held a research staff post at Visva-Bharati University.
Shantu Barua specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University (attested 2015) and served as an Associate Professor at the University of Dhaka in 2020.

Shaoyong Ye works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his doctoral studies at Peking University by 2009 under the supervision of Qing Duan, and later served as an Associate Professor (attested 2010-2016) and faculty member (attested 2026) there.
Sharad Deshpande specializes in philosophy and Indology. He earned his doctorate at Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1972 and later served as a Professor there (attested 2026).
Sharon J. Roe is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. She earned her PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2014) under doctoral supervisor Steven D. Goodman.

Sharon Salzberg is a Buddhist studies and religious studies practitioner and scholar who studied at the University at Buffalo (1969) and with traditional teachers. She co-founded the Insight Meditation Society (1974) and the Barre Center for Buddhist Studies (1989).

Shashibhusan Dasgupta (1911-1964) was an Indian scholar in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He completed an MA, studentship, and PhD at the University of Calcutta between 1933 and 1939, later serving as a Lecturer there (~1945-1964).

Shayne Clarke specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an MA from the University of Canterbury and a PhD from UCLA (2006) under Gregory Schopen. He is an Associate Professor at McMaster University and a Research Fellow at IIBS (attested 2026).

Shechen Gyaltsab (1871-1926) was an active figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous teachers, including Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and taught Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
Shechen Rabjam Rinpoche works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under his spiritual teacher, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and founded Karuna-Shechen in 2000.

Sheila Jasanoff studied at Radcliffe College, the University of Bonn, Harvard University, and Harvard Law School. She held posts at Cornell University (~1978-1998) and became a professor at Harvard University around 1998.

Shek-Wing Tam (1935-2024) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Dudjom Rinpoche and others. He founded the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Studies Association in North America and served as a professor at Renmin University of China (~2006).
